validated_results.title: Habitual Tea Consumption Reduces Prostate Cancer Risk in Vietnamese Men: a Case-Control Study.
validated_results.journal: Asian Pacific journal of cancer prevention : APJCP
validated_results.reason: This case-control study evaluates the association between habitual tea consumption and the risk of incident prostate cancer in Vietnamese men.

extraction.population: Men aged 64-75 years in Ho Chi Minh City

sample_size.location: Abstract - Materials and Methods; total_n derived from reported group counts 253 + 419 = 672

effect_size.excerpt: Compared to men drinking < 100 ml/day, the adjusted OR (95% CI) for PCa among those drinking 100-500 ml/day and > 500 ml/day were 0.52 (95% CI 0.35-0.79) and 0.30 (95% CI 0.18-0.48), respectively. Similar reductions in PCa risk were also found for drinking 1-5 cups and more than 5 cups of tea daily.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared to men drinking < 100 ml/day, the adjusted OR (95% CI) for PCa among those drinking 100-500 ml/day and > 500 ml/day were 0.52 (95% CI 0.35-0.79) and 0.30 (95% CI 0.18-0.48), respectively.

p_value.excerpt: Significant inverse dose-response relationships were also observed for years of drinking and number of cups consumed daily (P <0.01).
